sections.h2: Who sends and who values Sterling Heights tax bills?
sections.html:
Three offices touch a Sterling Heights bill. The Office of Treasury at 40555 Utica Road sends and collects current-year tax, with counter hours of 8:30 to 5:00 on weekdays. The Assessing Office sets values and logs ownership changes. Macomb County inherits any balance still open on March 1.

Tell the right desk when something changes. A new lender means a call to Treasury at 586-446-2780, while a transfer of ownership or a principal residence update goes to Assessing at 586-446-2340. Owners whose tax is escrowed see a marked courtesy copy, and the original goes to the escrow agent.

Each parcel gets two bills a year from the City Treasurer's Office.

sections.h2: When are Sterling Heights summer and winter taxes due?
sections.html:
Summer tax can be paid penalty-free beginning July 1 and ending the first business day of September. Winter tax has a window from December 1 to the last day of February. Bills for the summer go out in late June, and winter bills in late November.

Sterling Heights tax bill schedule and late charges, from the city's Property Tax Information page
BillMailedPayable without penaltyIf left unpaid
SummerLate JuneJuly 1 through the first business day in SeptemberOne-half of 1% per month after September 1 through the end of February
WinterLate NovemberDecember 1 through the end of FebruaryOn March 1, an added 3% interest, then transfer to Macomb County

Whatever remains on either bill on March 1 follows that path. From then on, and for any earlier-year bill, you pay at the Macomb County Building in Mount Clemens (phone 586-469-5190), where further penalties accrue.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Sterling Heights tax bill?
sections.html:
Choose by how close the deadline is: a reply envelope arrives with the bill, and the city adds drop boxes, a card line and eCheck.

  • Mail a check made out to City of Sterling Heights in the supplied envelope, which is addressed to a Chicago post office box, with the parcel ID on the check.
  • Drop it in a secured box on the city center campus, either by the Police Department entrance or by the Utica entrance to City Hall.
  • Use a card at 877-495-2729 or on the payment website. Point and Pay adds a convenience fee, and American Express is declined.
  • Draw on a checking or savings account through the eCheck choice on that website.

Water and sewer bills can end up here too. Treasury says delinquent utility accounts are transferred to the tax rolls twice a year after City Manager approval. A seller with a past-due utility account should settle it before closing so it never lands on a tax bill.

sections.h2: How does a sale change taxable value in Sterling Heights?
sections.html:
Assessing works out assessed value, half of true cash value, from a two-year sales study. Voters passed Proposal A on March 15, 1994, which added taxable value: the smaller of state equalized value and a capped value. The cap is the prior year's taxable value grown by inflation or 5%, whichever is lower, plus construction changes.

A transfer releases the cap. The next year, taxable value jumps to state equalized value with no ceiling, so the seller's old bill can sit far below the first bill the buyer sees. The price on one deed does not fix the new value, because the city adjusts land and building values citywide from the study period and avoids reassessing from a single transaction.

Long-time owners should warn buyers about that first bill. Filing falls to the buyer: Property Transfer Affidavit form 2766, delivered to Assessing inside 45 days.

sections.h2: How do appeals and the Principal Residence Exemption work in Sterling Heights?
sections.html:
The yearly Notice of Assessment, Taxable Valuation, and Property Classification normally goes out on the final day of February. March Board of Review sessions usually open the third Monday of the month, with two panels of three city residents hearing appeals on value, classification and hardship. Written answers reach appellants by the first Monday in June, and an unhappy residential owner can next petition the Michigan Tax Tribunal.

  • Principal Residence Exemption: if the notice shows 0%, file form 2368 with Assessing by June 1 to affect the summer levy or by November 1 to affect the winter levy.
  • Rescission: an owner who stops living in the house must file form 2602 to end the exemption.
  • Tax information lookup: the city posts an online property tax lookup.

sections.h2: What is Sterling Heights like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Sterling Heights, a second-ring suburb in Macomb County, lies 14 to 20 miles north of downtown Detroit. Its 36 or so square miles of land include a corner crossed by the Clinton River. Until the 1950s it was Sterling Township, farmland known for rhubarb, and it became a city in 1968. The word Heights was added to the name to avoid a clash with the village of Sterling in Arenac County.

Growth came with the auto plants. Chrysler and Ford jobs drew families through the 1960s and 1970s, and Lakeside Mall opened in 1976. Many residents are Chaldean and Assyrian, and the area around 15 Mile Road and Ryan has the nickname Little Nineveh. Two freeways frame the city, M-53 (Van Dyke) and M-59 (Hall Road), with Mound Road running north and south and the mile roads from 14 Mile to 20 Mile crossing east to west.

Two school districts split the city: Utica Community Schools covers the northern half, with Stevenson and Henry Ford II high schools, and Warren Consolidated Schools covers the southern half, with Sterling Heights High School. Winters are cold, with 39.1 days a year when the temperature stays below freezing, which is worth remembering when buyers inspect roofs and basements.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Sterling Heights homes?
sections.html:
A mid-2025 Census estimate puts 133,931 people in the city, across 51,736 households of 2.57 people on average. Three in four homes (75.8%) are owner-occupied, with a median value of $274,300 and median gross rent of $1,292 in the 2020 to 2024 data.

Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,681, and those without report $666. Household income has a median of $79,909 in 2024 dollars. Ask Assessing for numbers on your own parcel, since a citywide median says little about one street.

The same survey shows 3,686.5 people per square mile in 2020, 28.0% of residents born abroad and 35.2% of people age five and older speaking a language other than English at home. About 31.1% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay Sterling Heights summer tax without a penalty?
faqs.a: The last day is the first business day in September. After September 1, the city adds one-half of 1% per month through the end of February.

faqs.q: Where does my Sterling Heights tax go if I miss the February deadline?
faqs.a: It goes to Macomb County. On March 1 the city adds 3% interest and transfers any balance on a summer or winter bill, and payment is then made at the Macomb County Building, 1 South Main, Mount Clemens, at 586-469-5190.

faqs.q: Who files the transfer affidavit after a Sterling Heights sale?
faqs.a: The buyer does. Form 2766 goes to the Assessing Office inside 45 days, and blank copies are on hand at the office and on the city and state Treasury websites.

faqs.q: How do I end the exemption after moving out of a Sterling Heights house?
faqs.a: Send the Assessing Office a Request to Rescind Homeowner's Principal Residence Exemption, form 2602. A buyer moving in files form 2368, with deadlines of June 1 for the summer levy and November 1 for the winter.

faqs.q: Can I pay Sterling Heights property tax by phone?
faqs.a: Yes. Call 877-495-2729 to pay by card, and expect a convenience fee from Point and Pay. American Express is not accepted. The payment website also takes eCheck payments from a checking or savings account.
